# Vendored dependency provenance

Third-party code checked into this repository, and where it came from. Nothing
here is fetched at build time — `vendor/` is committed on purpose so a clone
builds with no network access and no submodule initialisation for these files.

## doctest

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Path | `vendor/doctest/include/doctest/doctest.h` |
| Version | 2.4.11 (`DOCTEST_VERSION_MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH`, lines 49–51 of the header) |
| Upstream | https://github.com/doctest/doctest |
| Release tag | `v2.4.11` — note the leading `v`; the tag `2.4.11` does not exist |
| Upstream file | `doctest/doctest.h` (the single-header distribution) |
| Copyright | © 2016–2023 Viktor Kirilov |
| Licence | MIT |
| Size | 7106 lines, 321644 bytes |
| SHA-256 | `44faa038e9c3f9728efbda143748d01124ea0a27f4bf78f35a15d8fab2e039fb` |

The vendored copy is byte-for-byte identical to the upstream release. This was
verified, not assumed — see below.

### Why it is vendored

The project commits its dependencies rather than pulling them at configure
time, so that a fresh clone builds with nothing but a compiler, CMake, GLM, and
GLFW available. This also keeps the unit-test target buildable in an offline
or air-gapped environment.

### How to verify this copy is unmodified

The header is committed verbatim, so its digest is the check:

```bash
shasum -a 256 vendor/doctest/include/doctest/doctest.h   # macOS
sha256sum vendor/doctest/include/doctest/doctest.h       # Linux
```

To confirm the vendored copy against the upstream release:

```bash
curl -sL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/doctest/doctest/v2.4.11/doctest/doctest.h \
  | shasum -a 256
# 44faa038e9c3f9728efbda143748d01124ea0a27f4bf78f35a15d8fab2e039fb
```

The two digests must match. If they do not, the vendored file has been edited
and the difference is worth understanding before it is overwritten — the test
target compiles it directly, so a local modification would be invisible to
`ctest`.

The header itself carries `DO NOT MODIFY THIS FILE BY HAND - IT IS AUTO
GENERATED BY CMAKE!`, which is a second reason to treat any divergence as a
problem to investigate rather than a patch to keep.

### Upgrading

1. Replace `vendor/doctest/include/doctest/doctest.h` with the new release's
   single-header file.
2. Update the version, digest, line count, and copyright range in this file.
3. Build and run the suite: `ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure`.

A major-version bump is the one to watch: doctest has changed assertion macros
between major versions, and the suite in `tests/` is the thing that will tell
you.
